title: Customer Support Specialist
description:
This role is located onsite in Littleton, CO.

About Emporia Energy

Emporia is a leading technology company revolutionizing home energy by providing affordable, integrated solutions that empower homeowners to optimize energy usage to reduce costs and carbon footprint. Emporia’s Home Energy Management Platform is a powerful software system that connects their Vue Home Energy Monitor, Level 2 EV Charger, Smart Plugs, Home Battery, and third-party thermostats and appliances. By automating energy use through real-time monitoring and scheduling, the platform optimizes consumption, reduces costs, and simplifies home energy management—all within one intuitive app. With over 400,000 U.S. homes running Emporia’s energy management and EV charging hardware, we are now launching a national Third-Party Owned (TPO) home battery Virtual Power Plant — placing industrial-rated home batteries in residential homes to deliver power redundancy, utility cost savings, and grid peak demand services. By reducing energy waste and saving customers money, we’re helping create a healthier planet and a brighter future. For more information, visit emporiaenergy.com.

Mission, Vision and Values

Emporia was founded in 2018 with a clear purpose to revolutionize home energy, generate tangible customer savings, and accelerate the transition to a lower carbon future. We are striving to become the world's leading home energy management platform and build the largest virtual power plant.

  • Customers First: We deliver exceptional service with empathy and responsiveness, building lasting trust in every interaction.
  • Own the Outcome: We think like owners, taking responsibility for results and holding ourselves and each other accountable.
  • Win Together: We succeed together through honesty, humility and humanity.
  • Grit Gets it Done: We work hard, stay passionate, and persevere through challenges.
  • Better Every Day: We challenge the status quo, take smart risks and aim to improve 1% every day.

Role Overview and Responsibilities

We handle hundreds of daily support requests through various channels, including phone, in-app/web chat, email, web form submissions, and social media. These range from pre-sales questions about how our products work to live diagnostics and troubleshooting of devices. It is essential to have an understanding and empathetic voice when communicating with customers, especially those who require additional support due to a suboptimal experience with our product. Most communications relate to the specific behavior of our products, but some general questions about power/energy, residential electrical systems, and Internet of Things-related topics will also be submitted. As we continue to grow the company and expand our product portfolio, some of the additional customer discussion topics will include electric vehicles, home batteries, residential solar production, and more.

As the primary point of communication between the company and its customers, we often serve as the voice of the company, providing feedback and customer experience insights to team members. Emporia Energy is focused on delivering an exceptional customer experience. Every team member is dedicated to assisting the support team with any questions, walkthroughs, explanations of the product, and technical details. We’re not looking for an expert in electrical engineering or software development; we're looking for an individual excited about joining a growing technology company that aims to make its mark on the energy industry and ensure our customers have the best experience available.

It’s common to hear Emporia's CEO mention that Customer Support is the most critical team in the company. Don’t believe us? It’s painted on the walls of our office. We consider the happiness of our customers to be our top priority and provide the Customer Support team with all the necessary resources to make that happen.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Strong communication skills
    • Reading: Comprehending customer requests, understanding problems and potential troubleshooting steps with limited information provided by customers.
    • Writing: Sending dozens of written messages daily to customers and non-customers via chat/email/messaging systems.
    • Phone/Speaking: Ability to communicate with customers worldwide and discuss technical details (no secondary language/translation skills required).
  • Comfortable with technology, including Smartphones/Apps, Web and Web applications, “Cloud”-based services, WiFi, and IoT (Internet of Things). Detailed technical experience is not required, but you should be flexible and eager to learn the specific aspects of the job position.
  • Full-time, on-site presence required
  • Hours of operation: 8-5/M-F (subject to change as business needs dictate)

What We Offer

💰 Compensation: $25.00 per hour starting pay.

🏥 Benefits: medical/dental/vision insurance, 401(k), employee stock option program, paid holidays plus unlimited PTO, discounts on Emporia products and partner offerings.

📈 Career Growth: Be part of a fast-growing company at the forefront of home energy innovation.

A resume is required to be considered for this position.

New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check.

Note: Applicants must have authorization to work with the U.S. without sponsorship. Sponsorship for this position is not available.

Any communication to applicants relating to the Emporia Energy hiring process will only come from email addresses with the domains emporiaenergy.com or no-reply@us.greenhouse-mail.io. If in the course of the application or hiring process with Emporia Energy you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact cybersecurity@emporiaenergy.com.

Emporia Energy is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, service in the military, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. We will make reasonable accommodations for any qualified applicant with a disability, provided that the individual is otherwise qualified to safely perform the essential functions of the job with or without accommodation and that the accommodation would not impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. Please let us know if you believe you require reasonable accommodation, or if you would like assistance to complete an application or to participate in an interview at the company.

title: Hardware Product Lead - AI Builder - Home Energy Products
description:
Reports to: SVP, Product
Location: Onsite in Littleton, CO

About Emporia Energy

Emporia is a leading technology company revolutionizing home energy by providing affordable, integrated solutions that empower homeowners to optimize energy usage to reduce costs and carbon footprint. Emporia’s Home Energy Management Platform is a powerful software system that connects their Vue Home Energy Monitor, Level 2 EV Charger, Smart Plugs, Home Battery, and third-party thermostats and appliances. Mission, Vision and Values

Emporia was founded in 2018 with a clear purpose to revolutionize home energy, generate tangible customer savings, and accelerate the transition to a lower carbon future. We are striving to become the world's leading home energy management platform and build the largest virtual power plant.

  • Customers First: We deliver exceptional service with empathy and responsiveness, building lasting trust in every interaction.
  • Own the Outcome: We think like owners, taking responsibility for results and holding ourselves and each other accountable.
  • Win Together: We succeed together through honesty, humility and humanity.
  • Grit Gets it Done: We work hard, stay passionate, and persevere through challenges.
  • Better Every Day: We challenge the status quo, take smart risks and aim to improve 1% every day.

Role Overview

Emporia's home energy products are already in hundreds of thousands of homes: our Level 2 EV chargers, the Vue Energy Monitor, and the Smart Plug. They earn revenue today, they sit in competitive categories, and they carry the install base everything else builds on. This role owns all three.

This is not a new-product job. The work is keeping a mature portfolio healthy, competitive, and profitable: field quality, cost, supply continuity, incremental revisions, and the eventual end-of-life call. The Product Lead is the DRI, the single-person decision maker for product definition, development, and launch. They do not necessarily do all the work, but they ensure the work gets done. Where this description says "own," it means accountable for the decision and the outcome, not doing the work alone. On this portfolio that means every change that ships, from a firmware release to a board revision to a price move. Operations and Sustaining run field service, RMA processing, and production; you own the product decisions behind them.

You report to SVP Product. Revisions and new SKUs still move through the same product development lifecycle (PDLC) as any new product, just in shorter cycles. We move quickly by being disciplined, not by skipping process. The same stage-gates and deliverables stay in place: PRD, PCD, business case, design reviews, launch readiness. AI should accelerate the work to be done and minimize and remove hand offs along the way.

Responsibilities

Portfolio & Roadmap: Owning What Ships

Own the roadmap across all three lines and the prioritization between them.

  • Own the roadmap for EVSE, Vue, and Smart Plug, and make the call on where effort goes when all three want the same engineering week.
  • Own competitive positioning and pricing in crowded categories, tracking what competitors ship and what it means for our roadmap.
  • Build the business case for every change you propose, with AI as-needed: cost, margin, volume, and payback.
  • Turn support tickets, telemetry, reviews, and RMA data into a ranked list of what to fix and what to build, using AI to read the volume rather than sampling it.

Field Quality & Sustaining: The Core of the Job

Shipping products fail in the field, and the product side owns the answer to why.

  • Own the sustaining roadmap: firmware releases, field-quality issues, and warranty and reliability trends feeding back into requirements.
  • Drive root cause on field failures with Engineering, Quality, and Customer Support, and decide what gets fixed in firmware, in hardware, or in documentation.
  • Partner with Customer Support so the top drivers of contacts and returns get engineered out, not just answered faster.
  • Use AI to close knowledge gaps in failure data, logs, and schematics, so your discussions with subject matter experts start further along.

Cost, Supply & Compliance

On mature products, margin and continuity are where the leverage is.

  • Drive cost-down: component substitutions, design-for-cost changes, and supplier negotiation, protecting margin as categories get more competitive.
  • Stay ahead of component obsolescence and single-source risk, qualifying replacements and second sources before they become urgent.
  • Drive compliance continuity with Engineering and Compliance, including recertification when a component or design changes (UL, FCC, Energy Star, and others as they apply).
  • Work with Operations on volume planning, yield, and quality so supply keeps up with demand.

Revisions, New SKUs & EOL

Incremental releases are still real product launches, just faster.

  • Define and drive hardware revisions, new variants, and SKU additions through the same gates, at a cycle time that fits the size of the change.
  • Write the requirements, negotiate scope and timeline with Engineering and Operations to a shared commitment, and make the final call on when and how each change ships.
  • Own launch and go-to-market for revisions and new SKUs working with Marketing, BD, and Customer Support, including channel and support readiness.
  • Own end-of-availability and end-of-life decisions, with a transition plan for customers and channel.

Driving AI Adoption: Across Every Phase

Native AI-use runs through the whole job. Gates, deliverables, and approvals stay in place. The waiting between them goes. Push that on the team, not just yourself.

  • Automate and optimize the manual, slow, or expensive steps you find in the PDLC. Push yourself and the broader team to challenge the default approach without diluting the deliverable.
  • Use AI to build at the edge of capability. Exemplify AI-enabled execution, encouraging Engineering, Operations, and partners to push past their traditional approach and deliver faster.
  • Build and share your own tools, prompts, and workflows instead of asking for headcount.
  • Be honest about where AI is not working, and feed real evidence back into how Emporia adopts it.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • 5+ years in product management for hardware, including real ownership of shipping products and not only new product introduction.
  • A track record as a DRI, accountable for outcomes and not just definition, comfortable with ambiguity and parallel workstreams.
  • Experience owning sustaining work: field quality, warranty and RMA analysis, firmware release decisions, and root cause with engineering.
  • A track record of cost-down and margin improvement on products already in production.
  • Experience with component obsolescence, second sourcing, and supply continuity.
  • Comfort with competitive and pricing decisions in a crowded consumer category.
  • Heavy, fluent use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or similar), plus a habit of building your own tooling instead of asking for headcount, and getting others to adopt it.
  • Business sense: you can own a business case, unit economics, and margin trade-offs leadership will bet on.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership: you lead through influence and escalate well without formal reporting authority.
  • Experience running a formal gate process for hardware, and a belief that discipline is what makes speed possible.

Desired Qualifications & Skills

  • EV charging, energy monitoring, smart plugs, or other connected home hardware.
  • Consumer electronics sold at retail and direct-to-consumer scale.
  • Recertification experience (UL, FCC, Energy Star) after design or component changes.
  • High-volume manufacturing quality work: DPPM, FAI, yield, and RMA analysis.
  • Fleet telemetry and cohort analysis on a large install base.
  • A career spanning both product management and program management, in a fast-paced, test and validation driven environment.

What We Offer

💰 Compensation: The expected base salary range is $130,000 - $170,000, plus stock options. The offered salary will depend on numerous factors, including but not limited to work experience, skills, and internal equity considerations. The base salary does not include benefits or other incentives.

🏥 Benefits: medical/dental/vision insurance, 401(k), employee stock option program, paid holidays plus unlimited PTO, discounts on Emporia products and partner offerings.

title: Hardware Product Lead: V2X DC Bidirectional Charging
description:
Reports to: SVP of Product
Location: Onsite in Boulder or Littleton, CO

About Emporia Energy

Emporia is a leading technology company revolutionizing home energy by providing affordable, integrated solutions that empower homeowners to optimize energy usage to reduce costs and carbon footprint. Emporia’s Home Energy Management Platform is a powerful software system that connects their Vue Home Energy Monitor, Level 2 EV Charger, Smart Plugs, Home Battery, and third-party thermostats and appliances. By automating energy use through real-time monitoring and scheduling, the platform optimizes consumption, reduces costs, and simplifies home energy management—all within one intuitive app. With over 400,000 U.S. homes running Emporia’s energy management and EV charging hardware, we are now launching a national Third-Party Owned (TPO) home battery Virtual Power Plant — placing industrial-rated home batteries in residential homes to deliver power redundancy, utility cost savings, and grid peak demand services. By reducing energy waste and saving customers money, we’re helping create a healthier planet and a brighter future. For more information, visit emporiaenergy.com.

Mission, Vision and Values

Emporia was founded in 2018 with a clear purpose to revolutionize home energy, generate tangible customer savings, and accelerate the transition to a lower carbon future. We are striving to become the world's leading home energy management platform and build the largest virtual power plant.

  • Customers First: We deliver exceptional service with empathy and responsiveness, building lasting trust in every interaction.
  • Own the Outcome: We think like owners, taking responsibility for results and holding ourselves and each other accountable.
  • Win Together: We succeed together through honesty, humility and humanity.
  • Grit Gets it Done: We work hard, stay passionate, and persevere through challenges.
  • Better Every Day: We challenge the status quo, take smart risks and aim to improve 1% every day.

Role Overview

Emporia's DC bidirectional program pairs white-labeled power electronics from an inverter supplier with the Vehicle Integration Board, the piece Emporia designs in-house. The design is in-flight. It needs one clear owner to drive it through validation, certification, and launch: the supplier on one side, our own board development on the other.

Every Emporia hardware product moves through the same product development lifecycle (PDLC): Concept, Feasibility, EVT, DVT, PVT, Launch & Ramp, and Sustaining/EOL. This program is already well into design, so the weight of this role sits from EVT forward: program management, execution, and go-to-market rather than early concept work. The Product Lead is the DRI, the single-person decision maker for product definition, development, and launch. They do not necessarily do all the work, but they ensure the work gets done. Where this description says "own," it means accountable for the decision and the outcome, not doing the work alone. AI is what lets one person cover this much ground: draft the PRD and business case yourself, build initial concepts and designs, then spend your time on what AI cannot touch, like OEM and utility negotiations, certification, gate reviews, and unblocking the team.

You report to SVP Product and own the program from here through Launch & Ramp, then hand the DRI role to Operations and Sustaining, moving into a supporting role. Bidirectional charging only works when the vehicle, the home, and the utility all cooperate, so launch depends as much on automotive OEM approval and utility interconnection as on the hardware. We move quickly by being disciplined, not by skipping process. The same stage-gates and deliverables stay in place: PRD, PCD, business case, design reviews, launch readiness. AI should accelerate the work to be done and minimize and remove hand offs along the way.

Responsibilities

Definition & Business Case: Closing Out Concept
The concept is largely set. Your job here is to close the gaps and own the numbers.

  • Take over the PRD and PCD, close the open requirements, and lock the interface between the supplier's power electronics and our Vehicle Integration Board.
  • Own the business case and unit economics yourself, with AI as-needed: supplier cost, board cost, installed cost, and the price the market will carry.
  • Keep competitive positioning current and recommend go/no-go at each remaining stage gate.

Program Delivery: EVT, DVT & PVT
The center of the job. Own getting it built, validated, and certified on schedule.

  • Own the schedule and gate reviews across the inverter supplier, our in-house board development, test, and Operations, holding the critical path in one place.
  • Work with Manufacturing Operations to hold the inverter supplier to specs, cost, quality, schedule, and roadmap.
  • Drive the Vehicle Integration Board through development and validation: electrical, firmware, bring-up, and test.
  • Drive the safety and interconnection path with Engineering and Compliance, including where the supplier's certifications end and system-level listing begins: UL 9741, ISO 15118, IEEE 1547, UL 1741 SB, and the labs and AHJ dialogue. Know what their platform can and cannot do before committing to it.
  • Drive automotive OEM engagement to a validated, approved vehicle list at launch, including compatibility testing and each OEM's own approval process.
  • Work utility interconnection in every launch territory, and unblock the program yourself rather than waiting for someone else to raise it.

Launch: Mass Production Ramp & Go-to-Market
Get the product to market and selling. This is the last phase you own outright.

  • Own go-to-market working with Marketing, BD, and Customer Support: positioning, pricing, launch messaging, and the installer and channel readiness the product needs to sell.
  • Land the OEM side of launch: the approved vehicle list, partner coordination, and clear customer-facing compatibility guidance.
  • Own the ramp: first installs, commissioning results, early field performance, and the go/no-go on scaling.
  • Make the final call on when and how it ships, then hand off to Operations and Sustaining with baseline metrics, known issues, and the rationale behind key decisions.

Sustaining & EOL: Supporting Role
After ramp, Operations and Sustaining own the product. Your role here reduces.

  • Be the person who knows why decisions were made. You are no longer the DRI.
  • Answer roadmap, customer-impact, and escalation questions when asked, supporting the resolution.
  • Carry field and quality lessons into your next program.

Driving AI Adoption: Across Every Phase
Native AI-use runs through the whole job. Gates, deliverables, and approvals stay in place. The waiting between them goes away. Push that on the team, not just yourself.

  • Automate and optimize the manual, slow, or expensive steps you find in the PDLC. Push yourself and the broader team to challenge the default approach without diluting the deliverable.
  • Use AI to build at the edge of capability. Exemplify AI-enabled execution, encouraging Engineering, Operations, and partners to push past their traditional approach and deliver faster.
  • Build and share your own tools, prompts, and workflows instead of asking for headcount.
  • Be honest about where AI is not working, and feed real evidence back into how Emporia adopts it.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • 5+ years across product management and program or delivery management for hardware, with full ownership through launch.
  • Strong program management across a mixed build: experience holding a white-label, ODM, or contract partner to specs, cost, and schedule while an in-house team delivers a critical component.
  • A track record as a DRI, accountable for outcomes and not just definition, comfortable with ambiguity and parallel workstreams, and willing to hand off cleanly at ramp.
  • Experience with EV charging, power electronics, inverters, or other grid-connected hardware.
  • Experience in a certification-heavy environment, and comfort owning a safety and interconnection approval path end to end.
  • Experience working with automotive OEMs, utilities, or other institutional partners whose approval gates your launch.
  • Heavy, fluent use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or similar), plus a habit of building your own tooling instead of asking for headcount, and getting others to adopt it.
  • Business sense: you can own a business case, unit economics, and margin trade-offs leadership will bet on.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership: you lead through influence and escalate well without formal reporting authority.
  • Experience running a formal gate process for hardware, and a belief that discipline is what makes speed possible.

Desired Qualifications & Skills

  • DC fast charging, V2G, V2H, or other bidirectional charging products, and UL 9741, ISO 15118, IEEE 1547, or UL 1741 experience.
  • Automotive OEM program, validation, or homologation experience.
  • Utility interconnection or grid-services programs.
  • Owning a board-level design (electrical and firmware) through validation and production.
  • A career spanning both product management and program management, in a fast-paced, test and validation driven environment.

What We Offer

💰 Compensation: The expected base salary range is $145,000 - $190,000, plus stock options. The offered salary will depend on numerous factors, including but not limited to work experience, skills, and internal equity considerations. The base salary does not include benefits or other incentives.

🏥 Benefits: medical/dental/vision insurance, 401(k), employee stock option program, paid holidays plus unlimited PTO, discounts on Emporia products and partner offerings.

Emporia is a leading technology company revolutionizing home energy by providing affordable, integrated solutions that empower homeowners to optimize energy usage to reduce costs and carbon footprint. Emporia’s Home Energy Management Platform is a powerful software system that connects their Vue Home Energy Monitor, Level 2 EV Charger, Smart Plugs, Home Battery, and third-party thermostats and appliances. By automating energy use through real-time monitoring and scheduling, the platform optimizes consumption, reduces costs, and simplifies home energy management—all within one intuitive app. With over 400,000 U.S. homes running Emporia’s energy management and EV charging hardware, we are now launching a national Third-Party Owned (TPO) home battery Virtual Power Plant — placing industrial-rated home batteries in residential homes to deliver power redundancy, utility cost savings, and grid peak demand services. By reducing energy waste and saving customers money, we’re helping create a healthier planet and a brighter future. For more information, visit emporiaenergy.com.

Role Overview

Emporia Energy is seeking a strategic and results-driven Supply Chain and Cost Manager. This role focuses on optimizing our manufacturing partnerships and driving aggressive cost-down initiatives across our global supply chain, with deep ties to the consumer electronics manufacturing ecosystem. The candidate serves as the primary commercial and operational link between Emporia and our Contract Manufacturing (CM) partners, ensuring cost competitiveness and supply resilience.

Core Responsibilities & Coordination

Cost Management & Strategic Sourcing

  • Drive the “Cost Down” roadmap for core products, identifying savings in materials, labor, and process yield.
  • Run Quarterly Cost Reviews (QCR) with CM partners to track commodity indices and intercept cost creep early.
  • Manage the competitive reality of dual-sourcing to influence volume allocation and drive pricing leverage.
  • Initiate value engineering exercises with engineering teams to unlock meaningful cost reductions in the pipeline.
  • Establish incentive structures for shared cost savings between Emporia and manufacturing partners.
  • Consolidate CM quote comparisons into interactive dashboards to strengthen negotiating positions.
  • Monitor global trade factors, such as tariff re-evaluations, and their impact on COGS and sourcing strategy.

Supply Chain Operations

  • Establish direct sourcing relationships with vendors to provide to our CM partners
  • Oversee supplier base ownership, ensuring operational depth in material planning and NPI handoffs.
  • Align build plans with 12-month rolling forecasts to optimize inventory held by suppliers on behalf of Emporia with the Operations team.

Cross-Functional & General

  • Ad hoc analysis and other miscellaneous tasks as assigned.
  • Identify and drive business process improvements and coordinate with other teams to implement.
  • Lead the design and development of a custom, in-house ERP platform rather than purchasing off-the-shelf software; leverage an AI-native working style to accelerate requirements drafting, system architecture, and technical documentation for this custom build.
  • Emporia is a startup — this role requires wearing many hats, and this description does not capture every assignment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering or equivalent education / work experience.
  • In-depth knowledge of electronics and mechanical supply chain management & components
  • Proven track record of cost-down execution, strategic sourcing, and managing complex vendor relationships in a high-growth, consumer electronics or hardware manufacturing environment.
  • Experience working with overseas ODM/CM contract manufacturers and suppliers at scale; experience with partners in India is a plus.
  • Strong cross-functional relationship-building skills across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Ability to travel internationally to contract manufacturing partners and suppliers, up to approximately 20% of the time.
  • AI-native working style: comfortable using AI tools to accelerate product research, ingest and synthesize data across multiple platforms and systems, and draft requirements and documentation.
